title: Macroeconomics
tagline: National income in the long run, money and inflation, unemployment, consumption and investment, IS–LM and aggregate demand, aggregate supply and the Phillips curve, stabilisation and public debt
summary: Macroeconomics studies the economy as a whole: output, unemployment, inflation and interest rates, and the policies that affect them. This course builds the standard intermediate models — the classical long-run model, money and inflation, the labour market, consumption and investment, IS–LM, aggregate supply and the Phillips curve — and uses them to analyse stabilisation policy, budget deficits and government debt.

chapters.title: National income in the long run
chapters.summary: Output, factor prices and the distribution of income in the classical model, and how saving and investment determine the real interest rate.

chapters.title: Money and inflation
chapters.summary: The quantity theory of money, seigniorage, the Fisher effect, the costs of inflation and hyperinflation.

chapters.title: Unemployment and the labour market
chapters.summary: Job finding and job separation, the natural rate of unemployment, frictional and structural unemployment, and wage rigidity.

chapters.title: Consumption and saving
chapters.summary: From the Keynesian consumption function to intertemporal choice, the permanent-income and life-cycle hypotheses, and Ricardian equivalence.

chapters.title: Investment
chapters.summary: Business fixed investment and the user cost of capital, Tobin’s q, residential investment and inventories.

chapters.title: Aggregate demand: the IS–LM model
chapters.summary: The Keynesian cross, equilibrium in the goods and money markets, and the effects of fiscal and monetary policy on output and interest rates.

chapters.title: Aggregate supply and the Phillips curve
chapters.summary: Short-run aggregate supply, sticky prices and wages, the Phillips curve, expectations and the costs of disinflation.

chapters.title: Stabilisation policy
chapters.summary: The AD–AS model in action, demand and supply shocks, policy lags, rules versus discretion, and the Lucas critique.

chapters.title: Fiscal policy and government debt
chapters.summary: Budget deficits, the government budget constraint, the dynamics of the debt ratio, and the debate over the burden of public debt.
